messages.subject: question from a graduate
messages.body_plain:
hello Dr：
my name is xia xiao, i am a graduate from Northwest A&F university,China.recently, i have used the methylkit software to find out DMR(different methylation region),but i have meet several problem.
here is my protocal:
1. use bismark to generate sam file and use the samtools to sort the sam files
2. use the processBismarkAl command and generate CpG.txt file
here is part of my result,after that, i found it is a little bit different compared with the result(contained in the methylkit package),which is ,so i add the "chr" to row chrBase and row chr, and the result turned in to this one it still looks a little bit different with the official results. and when i use the command it gives me such ERR message : character vector parameters are required. i really do not know which mistakes do i made? could you please give me some advice? i am really need your help.
best wishes
xia xiao

messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Unite Error
messages.body_plain:
You can try to use Unix tools such as sort and uniq to find duplicated coordinates, you need to extract just the coordinates part of the files first. Please do share if you track this bug on the Bismark side

On Dec 20, 2018 6:07 PM, <chri...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi all,
>
> I am trying to use methylkit to analyze WGBS data. I have loaded my 12 samples successfully from Bismark .cov file:
> myobj=methRead(file.list, pipeline="bismarkCoverage",
>                sample.id <http://sample.id>=list("conc0s1","conc0s2","conc0s3","conc0.3s1","conc0.3s2", "conc0.3s3", "conc3s1","conc3s2", "conc3s3", "conc30s1","conc30s2", "conc30s3"),
>                assembly="z11",
>                treatment=c(0,0,0,1,1,1,2,2,2,3,3,3),
>                context="CpG"
> )
> but when trying to unite them, I get the following error:
>
> meth=unite(myobj,destrand = FALSE)
> Error in vecseq(f__, len__, if (allow.cartesian || notjoin || !anyDuplicated(f__,  :
>   Join results in 4387096 rows; more than 1399355 = nrow(x)+nrow(i). Check for duplicate key values in i each of which join to the same group in x over and over again. If that's ok, try by=.EACHI to run j for each group to avoid the large allocation. If you are sure you wish to proceed, rerun with allow.cartesian=TRUE. Otherwise, please search for this error message in the FAQ, Wiki, Stack Overflow and data.table issue tracker for advice.
>
>
> It seems like there is duplicate coordinates in my data, if so how can I fix this? Thank you for any help.
>
>
